Badr El Hammami 
Thabrate, 2010-2018 
Sound installation, photographic transfer to cassettes, headphones, MP3 players 
Variable dimensions 

Courtesy of the Musée national de l’histoire de l’immigration 

How to safeguard the essence of orality at a distance? How to keep in touch when one cannot write? How not to forget the feel of one’s mother tongue on their lips? Started in 2010, Thabrate, translating to “letter” in Berber, is a project inspired by a correspondence practice which took place between the 1970s and 1980s among Moroccan immigrant workers and their families left behind in Morocco. With illiteracy then widespread and the telephone not yet democratized, the audio cassette became the tool to deliver messages across borders, accompanied at times by photographs and small documents.

The work reproduces such a magnetic correspondence, exchanged thirty years later between Badr El Hammami and his friend Fadma Kadourri.

Majd Abdel Hamid 
Polaroids, Muscle Memory (set D), 2022 

In his multimedia practice, Majd Abdel Hamid reclaims embroidery, a traditional craft inherited from his Palestinian heritage, as a radical means of expression, and Muscle Memory is a tribute to the city that has adopted him: Beirut. 

Exhausting his restless fingers into a comforting habit, he tries to find a pattern that could represent Beirut just as each Palestinian embroidered pattern corresponds to a region there. 

The series, including iPhone photographs transferred onto Polaroid paper, materializes as a subjective wandering through a scarred urban landscape that has nonetheless become a refuge for the Palestinian artist.

HYPERCULTE
LIVE CONCERT

Formed in 2013, the Swiss duo Hyperculte, composed of Simone Aubert and Vincent Bertholet, brings together disco, pop, krautrock, punk and post-rock in a distinctive and energetic sound.

Driven by sharp rhythms, musical improvisation and politically engaged lyrics, their work moves between experimentation, poetry and a powerful reflection on the world around us.

PAULO NAZARETH
Cinema Tropical, 2025
Multimedia installation: video projection, posters, lightboxes, photographs.

Courtesy of the artist, Mendes Wood DM, Kamel Lazaar Foundation & Centre d’Art Contemporain Genève for BIM’26.

In Wale Man, a man spends his time waiting for a whale to die by his side. While he waits, he carries out different tasks, from going out to the open sea to fish, to staying on dry land to clean the beach and the desert.

@paulonazareth_official

MONA BENYAMIN
Unravel, 2026
Two-channel video installation, four-channel sound, 10’

Courtesy of the artist, Kamel Lazaar Foundation & Centre d’Art Contemporain Genève for BIM’26.

Unravel is a video installation in the form of a horror film that collapses into itself indefinitely. Across two video channels and four speakers, a shared musical score binds together two seemingly disparate worlds. On one screen, a choir performs a choral adaptation of Maurice Ravel’s Boléro, informed by Arabic vocal traditions and arranged by Manar Hashmi. The other screen features a horror-inflected narrative starring the artist’s parents, Michel and Nahia Benyamin. The conductor’s downbeat sends the choir into song and the couple into motion. As soon as the first note is heard, the couple steps out of a car to make their way home, pursued by a menacing camera and Boléro’s infamous crescendo. This chase grows increasingly threatening, culminating in a frenzied pursuit up a spiral staircase. Retour sur le vernissage de l’exposition ‘Contre;Courant’ au B7L9 Art Center (@b7l9_tunis), à Tunis !

L’exposition plonge les visiteurs dans l’univers de la Méditerranée, à travers les histoires de celles et ceux qui la traversent, la quittent ou y cherchent un refuge.

Entre mémoire, exil et espoir, elle invite à porter un autre regard sur cette mer et sur les destins qui s’y croisent.

A look back at the opening of the exhibition ‘Undertow’ at B7L9 Art Center (@b7l9_tunis), in Tunis!

The exhibition immerses visitors in the world of the Mediterranean through the stories of those who cross it, leave it behind or seek refuge within its shores.
Through memory, exile and hope, it invites us to look at this sea and the lives that intersect along its shores from a different perspective.

AKEN — A:/MATTER — PHASE I: LAYERED SYSTEM DYNAMICS

Join us at B7L9 Art Centre for the release party and immersive listening session of Aken’s debut album.

Recorded in his bedroom in La Marsa, the album brings four machines into conversation, exploring rhythms, loops and shifting patterns. Rather than composing melodies, Aken discovers them through improvisation, allowing the machines to shape the music as it unfolds.

Drawing on kosmische music, minimalism and the machine soul of Detroit, A:/MATTER is an invitation to experience sound as a living system.

Thursday, November 19

‏AKEN — A:/MATTER — PHASE I: LAYERED SYSTEM DYNAMICS

انضموا إلينا في مركز الفنون B7L9 للاحتفال بإطلاق ألبوم Aken الأول، من خلال جلسة استماع غامرة.

تم تسجيل الألبوم في غرفة نومه في المرسى، حيث تدخل أربع آلات موسيقية في حوار فيما بينها، مستكشفةً الإيقاعات والتكرارات والأنماط الموسيقية المتغيّرة. وبدلًا من تأليف الألحان بشكل تقليدي، يكتشفها Aken من خلال الارتجال، تاركًا للآلات المجال لتشكيل الموسيقى وتطويرها أثناء العزف.

يستمد ألبوم A:/MATTER إلهامه من موسيقى كوزميشه (Kosmische)، وموسيقى المينيماليزم (Minimalism)، والطابع الآلي المميّز لموسيقى ديترويت، ليقدّم تجربة تدعونا إلى الاستماع إلى الصوت باعتباره نظامًا حيًّا ومتغيّرًا.
